pages.text: $(bold)Building a base on another planet is a major infrastructure project.$()$(br2)You need breathable air, power, and supplies. This is where your T2-T4 tech investments pay off — players who built proper RF infrastructure will find space colonization much easier.

$(bold)Oxygen Distribution$()$(br)The $(bold)Oxygen Distributor$() creates a breathable zone around itself. It scales with area and requires $(italic)significant$() RF power. A single distributor covers a small room. A proper base needs multiple units.$(br2)$(bold)Water Pump$()$(br)Extracts water for conversion to oxygen. Place near ice deposits on Mars or bring water tanks.

$(bold)RF Power on Planets$()$(br)Ad Astra's built-in Coal Generator is intentionally weak. You $(italic)must$() bring real power infrastructure:$(br)• $(bold)Mekanism Generators$() — Fusion Reactor, Gas-Burning Generator$(br)• $(bold)Thermal Dynamos$() — Portable and reliable$(br)• $(bold)Flux Networks$() — The critical mod for cross-dimensional RF transfer$(br2)A Fusion Reactor powering a Moon base feels earned. A Coal Generator does not.

$(bold)Flux Networks — Your Best Friend$()$(br)Flux Networks is the $(italic)only$() way to wirelessly transmit RF across dimensions. A player who invested in Flux Networks during T2-T3 has a massive advantage for space exploration.$(br2)Set up a Flux Controller at your overworld base, then place Flux Points on each planet. Instant cross-dimensional wireless power. This is the intended solution for planetary base power.
